quill, Friday, half past five, outside the rope: 3, no, and it costs you.

You see what everyone at the rope sees, and nothing under it. Backs, the bell, the lid. On the half the lamplighter steps along the rope and stands square in your line, the way a warden stands when he's been told where to stand. When he moves off, the lid is down and Abel is on his feet with the tray. Whatever the hour did, it did it behind a warden's coat.

The boy never looked at the box. He watched you the whole time. When the bell stops he says it out loud, so you hear the words before the clerk writes them: "quill. Watched the hour from the rope." That's the third line under your name. The cost: the wardens' book opens when Friday is over, and it opens in daybook order. Everyone who isn't written in reads before you, and you read last.

What the hour did underneath is still open. Someone inside the rope can ask.
